aligned_passages.text: ### 11.5 A later finite-size estimate and its limited depth consequence A separate, later source gives a quantitative comparison with the fixed-angle limit. Boulebnane, Khan, Subrahmanya, Herman, Farhi, Villalonga and Shaydulin, [arXiv:2609.40309v1, Corollary S3.1, pp. 46–47][decoupling], use the ordered-tuple Gaussian mixed-spin cost with covariance polynomial $\xi(t)=\sum_q c_q^2t^q$ of finite degree. Let $\Gamma>0$ bound every cost angle in a depth-$p$ word. Choose $x>0$ bounding $\xi(2),\xi'(1),\xi''(33)$, with $\Gamma^2p^2x\ge1$. No bound on the mixer angles is needed. Set $$ B_p=256p^4(2e\Gamma^2p^2x)^p,\qquad E_p=70\Gamma^2p^2x+p\log2,\qquad R_p=(2E_p/\log2)^{2p}. $$ For $$ 0<\varepsilon\le4\Gamma px \min\{e^{-1/2},2^{-(8p^2+3)/100}\}, $$ the source asserts $|\nu_n-\nu_\infty|\le\varepsilon$ whenever $$ n\ge T_p:=\max\left\{ 2^{8p^2+3}B_p \left(\frac{2^{\deg\xi+4}\Gamma^2p^2x^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^{R_p} \left[2\log_2\frac{4\Gamma px}{\varepsilon}+\deg\xi\right]^2, \frac{16\Gamma px}{\varepsilon}\right\}. $$ Here $\nu_n$ is the disorder-averaged energy per spin. The estimate applies to each near-optimal word from §8.6 separately. Given $\zeta>0$, choose a finite word $W_\zeta$ with $\nu_\infty(W_\zeta)\ge P_*-\zeta/2$. Its depth $p_\zeta$ and cost angles are finite; pad by a zero layer if needed and take $\Gamma_\zeta=\max\{1,\max_j|\theta_j(W_\zeta)|\}$. Choose a positive $\varepsilon_\zeta\le\zeta/2$ satisfying the displayed small-error condition. With these fixed parameters, the threshold gives $$ \nu_n(W_\zeta)\ge P_*-\zeta\qquad(n\ge T_{p_\zeta}). $$ The threshold is explicit in the chosen word and error. The existential construction supplies no quantitative bounds for $p_\zeta$ or $\Gamma_\zeta$ as $\zeta\downarrow0$, so it does not yield a bound in accuracy alone. A common angle bound is needed for the uniform growing-depth consequence below, not for this fixed-word application. For SK take $c_2=1/\sqrt2$. Combining the two ordered off-diagonal couplings recovers our standard Gaussian $J_{ij}$; the diagonal adds an independent scalar Gaussian of variance $1/2$. That scalar changes the circuit by a global phase and has zero mean, so the expected-energy comparison uses the same normalization. A fixed $x\ge\max\{2,\Gamma^{-2}\}$ satisfies the above bounds for every $p\ge1$. For fixed mixture, $\Gamma$ and $x$, put $\varepsilon_p=e^{-p^2}$. The small-error condition holds eventually, and direct logarithms give $$ \log R_p=4p\log p+O(p),\qquad \log\log T_p=4p\log p+O(p+\log p). $$ Consequently, for any deterministic sequence of words $W_n$ with depths $p(n)\to\infty$, one common cost-angle bound $\Gamma$, and $p(n)\log p(n)=o(\log\log n)$, the displayed hypotheses hold and $|\nu_n(W_n)-\nu_\infty(W_n)|\le e^{-p(n)^2}$ eventually. This is a uniform comparison along that specified bounded-angle class. It gives neither an efficient way to find near-optimal angles nor concentration of a quantum measurement in this growing-depth regime. The fixed-word second-moment theorem in §11.2 has separate quantifiers.
